shortDescription: By Curtis WilliamsVenture Global NYSE:VG has asked the US Department of Energy for authorization to re-export liquefied natural gas from its CP2 LNG project in Louisiana as the company moves closer to bringing the first phase of the facility online, according to a notice from the DOE on Thursday.

children: has asked the US Department of Energy for authorization to re-export liquefied natural gas from its CP2 LNG project in Louisiana as the company moves closer to bringing the first phase of the facility online, according to a notice from the DOE on Thursday.

The second-largest LNG exporter in the US said it is seeking approval by January 15; it requested a blanket authorization to export previously imported LNG to countries that have free-trade agreements with the US as well as those that do not.

The company said the request would not require the construction of new facilities or any modifications to the terminal's operations. It also said exports conducted under the authorization would not exceed volumes already approved under its existing long-term export permits.

CP2, expected to become one of the largest LNG export facilities in the world, is already authorized to export up to 28 million metric tons per annum (mtpa) of LNG at peak capacity, and the company has applied to increase that level to 35 mtpa. Venture Global has also proposed a further expansion that would add another 10 mtpa of capacity.
